steps.body:
\[4x+3y=9,\qquad2x-2y=-13.\]

Use both equations.
steps.title: Solution | Step 1

steps.body:
Double the second equation: \(4x-4y=-26\). Subtract this from the first: \(7y=35\), so \(y=5\).

Equal x coefficients allow elimination.
steps.title: Solution | Step 2

steps.body:
\[2x-2(5)=-13\implies2x=-3\implies x=-\frac32.\]

Substitute back to find the other unknown.

Let the original sales be 100 units. After September they are \(100\times1.20=120\); after both months they are \(100\times0.90=90\).

Both overall percentages refer to the original sales.
steps.title: Solution | Step 1

steps.body:
\[x=\frac{120-90}{120}\times100=25.\]

The October decrease is measured relative to the September sales of 120.

steps.body:
\[V=(3x)(x)(13.5-2x)=40.5x^2-6x^3,\qquad0<x<6.75.\]

Multiply the three dimensions and require them all to be positive.
steps.title: Solution | Step 1

steps.body:
\[\frac{dV}{dx}=81x-18x^2=9x(9-2x).\]

Differentiate each power of x.
steps.title: Solution | Step 2

steps.body:
At a stationary point, \(9x(9-2x)=0\), giving \(x=0\) or \(x=4.5\). Only \(x=4.5\) is inside the domain.

A stationary volume has zero derivative.
steps.title: Solution | Step 3

steps.body:
The derivative is positive for \(0<x<4.5\) and negative for \(4.5<x<6.75\). Hence \(x=4.5\) gives the maximum.

The volume increases then decreases; its limiting endpoint volumes are zero.
steps.title: Solution | Step 4

steps.body:
\[V_{\max}=3(4.5)^2(13.5-9)=273.375\text{ cm}^3.\]

Substitute the maximising value into the original volume.

\[y=58-3\big((x-1)+4\big)^2=58-3(x+3)^2.\]

Use (a) with x replaced throughout by x-1.
steps.title: Part (b) | Step 1

steps.body:
Since \((x+3)^2\ge0\), the greatest y is 58, attained at \(x=-3\). Thus \(P=(-3,58)\).

The negative square term is largest when its square is zero.
steps.title: Part (b) | Step 2

steps.body:
The parabola is symmetric about its maximum, so its line of symmetry is \(x=-3\).

In 58-3(x+3)^2, equal positive and negative offsets from -3 give the same y.
